slides.title: Nature and the Environment
bullets: Prepare to read, discuss and write
slides.narration: Welcome to Grade 3 English, Unit 7: Nature and the Environment. Unit 7 follows Amal, Nora and Teacher Yasmin from the coast to the forest and up a mountain trail. Learners meet fifteen nature words, from climate and temperature to matter, energy and planet. They use the present perfect to say what they have seen, explored and visited, ask “Have you ever…?” questions, and build describing phrases such as “a metal rock on the beach”. The unit closes with clear instructions and a short poem about caring for our planet. In this short lecture, preview the key ideas and prepare for the independent lesson.

slides.title: What you will achieve
bullets: Name and describe the beach, the coast, the forest and the mountain using unit vocabulary.
Explain the difference between weather, climate and temperature, and describe today's weather.
Form present perfect sentences with have or has and the correct past participle.
slides.narration: By the end of this unit, you will be able to name and describe the beach, the coast, the forest and the mountain using unit vocabulary. You will also explain the difference between weather, climate and temperature, and describe today's weather. You will also form present perfect sentences with have or has and the correct past participle. Keep these goals in mind as you work.

slides.title: Language for precise thinking
slides.narration: Your vocabulary work begins with these words: climate, weather, temperature, sunshine, froze, mountain. Listen to each pronunciation in the vocabulary lab, study its meaning in context, and use the word accurately in your own discussion and writing.

slides.title: Read critically
slides.narration: The reading sequence includes Our Wonderful Nature and A Poem: “Nature Is Our Home”. Read actively. Identify each text's central ideas, notice viewpoint and reliability, and support every inference with relevant evidence from the text.

slides.title: The Present Perfect Tense
bullets: We use the present perfect for something that happened before but still matters today. When you say “I have explored a forest”, you tell people what your...
slides.narration: The first language focus is The Present Perfect Tense. We use the present perfect for something that happened before but still matters today. When you say “I have explored a forest”, you tell people what your life has already included. Notice the structure in the model examples, then apply it deliberately in connected sentences and paragraphs.

slides.title: Use English for a real purpose
bullets: Speaking 1 — Describe a Place in Nature
Writing 1 — Describe the Nature Near You
Explain, support and improve your ideas
slides.narration: In speaking, you will complete Speaking 1 — Describe a Place in Nature. Organise your ideas, use evidence and respond clearly to questions. In writing, you will plan, draft, check and revise. Use the success criteria before submitting your work.

slides.title: You are ready to begin
bullets: Activities, quiz and optional live sessions
slides.narration: You are ready to begin. Start with the vocabulary lab, continue through reading and comprehension, apply the grammar focus, and complete the speaking and writing practices. Use AI English for hints and feedback any time, and bring your questions to a live session too if you join one.
